title: UX Research Toolkit — Screens Layer
description: Layer schema extending each phase with the concrete product screens a persona passes through. This is the layer that turns a map from a research artefact into a reusable input: a screen carries a navigable route and an auth precondition, so an automated capturer can visit it and a test suite can derive scenarios from it without anyone re-typing the journey.
$comment:
WHY THIS LAYER EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT `touchpoints`.

`touchpoints` answers 'what does the persona interact with' in prose:
'App móvil', 'Correo de confirmación'. That is the right resolution for
research and the wrong one for automation, because prose does not resolve
to anything a machine can visit or assert against.

A screen is the same moment expressed so that BOTH readers work: a human
sees the step, and a capturer sees a route plus the auth state needed to
reach it. Nothing in this layer replaces `touchpoints`; a phase can carry
both, and a research-only map simply omits this one.

THE CONTRACT THE RENDERER MUST HOLD, stated here because it is the
property that makes a weekly pipeline survivable:

  A procedural wireframe renders UNDERNEATH the screenshot, always.

The screenshot is layered on top. When a capture is missing, stale or
failed, the wireframe stays visible and the map degrades to a diagram.
It never degrades to a broken image, and — more importantly — a missing
capture is VISIBLE as a wireframe rather than silently indistinguishable
from a captured one.

`code` is the join key and is never renumbered. The capturer writes
`<code>.jpg`, downstream suites key scenarios off the same string, and a
renumber would break both silently.

screens.description: Ordered product screens this phase passes through.

screen.description: One product screen: what it is called, where it lives, and what a visitor must already be to reach it.

code.description: Stable join key, unique across the whole map. Written by the capturer as `<code>.jpg` and consumed by downstream test suites. NEVER renumber it: a renumber orphans every capture and every derived scenario at once, and both fail silently.

label.description: Human-readable name for the screen, as it appears on the map.

path.description: Route relative to the product origin, with parameters in `:param` form. Must be navigable: this is what the capturer visits and what a `When` step would drive to. A path nobody can reach is a screen nobody can capture.

access.description:
The precondition a visitor must already satisfy to reach this screen. The capturer uses it to pick a session, and a derived test uses it to generate the authorization failure mode: for anything above `pub`, the first scenario is that a visitor WITHOUT it does not get there.

Ordered from least to most restrictive. The four in the middle are not decoration: collapsing them into `auth`/`admin` makes the capturer bring the wrong session, get a 403, and record a reachable screen as unreachable.

  pub    no session
  aware  reachable anonymously, personalised when signed in
  auth   any signed-in account
  ent    a purchased entitlement (an organization plan, a tier)
  ver    a verified or eligible state (accepted terms, joined the event)
  scoped a specific permission beyond plain admin
  admin  staff

MEASURED, not designed: this vocabulary was extracted from a real 195-screen map. The first draft of this schema had only four values, built from a sample of one lane, and the validator rejected 13 screens on the full map. That rejection is why the list is seven.

archetype.description: Layout family, used by the renderer to draw the procedural wireframe that sits underneath the screenshot. This is what makes a missing capture degrade to a diagram rather than to a broken image.

screenshot.description: Path or data URI of the captured image. OPTIONAL on purpose: a map with no captures is a valid map that renders as wireframes, and a pipeline that has not run yet must not invalidate the document it is supposed to enrich.

captured.description: When the screenshot was taken. Absence means never captured; a stale date means the capture is older than the screen. Both are legible states, and neither is the same as 'captured and fine' — which is the distinction a bare image silently loses.

pillar.description: Owning pillar, for routing findings to whoever can fix them. Left free-form here because the owning system is the consuming repo's, not this toolkit's: hard-coding one product's pillar list would make this schema wrong everywhere else.
